answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to deposit a unique behavioral pigment-a continuously updated, peer-attested history of distinctive decision traces that cannot be cheaply cloned. An attacker forging many identities must sustain parallel zephyr-like streams of original activity, each exposed to slashing if any fails a consistency check, driving the cost to the economic nadir where one failed cluster bankrupts the whole set.
